text_post: Unless you've been living in a cave for the last 40 years, I will assume you are aware of who Darth Vader is, and will not needlessly use the space to describe the story of the character. However, there is something that can be useful from reflecting upon the story of Darth Vader. A man who was so consumed with anger and rage that he was capable of committing atrocities so vile that people can generally agree that he needed to get help.  Yes, this is a purposefully severe understatement. Now why would I talk about this?  Because in my short time of trying to help inside the MHRM, I have noticed a lot of anger and rage among it's members. Some people might say something to the effect of "And what's wrong with being angry with the state of the world?"  To that, my answer is simply this:  Absolutely nothing.  However, if you allow yourself to be consumed by your anger, you run the risk of falling into that same trap as Vader. Anger is healthy.  It's an emotion used to understand when the boundaries that you set are being violated.  There is nothing wrong with that.  Every healthy person has boundaries. However, it also matters how it is expressed and how long you hold onto it. There is no known time frame for when it is no longer healthy to hold onto anger, however, that does not mean that a person cannot figure out for themselves when it has been held onto for too long. Some simple guidelines for when it might have been held onto for to long, and it is time to seek help, are as   follows: 1) When you wake up in the morning, and the first emotion you feel is anger. 2) Seeing things that make you angry, in even the smallest things. 3) Your first reaction to most things people say, is anger. 4) You lose your sense of compassion for others. 5) You catch people saying things like "S/He's always so angry.", "I think s/he is a great person, but I have trouble spending time with him/her, because of how angry s/he is.", or "I really don't know what is going to make him/her angry, and I don't like being around him/her." 6) If you believe any of the above statements are about you, that's a definite sign of needing help. The MHRM has a wonderful resource, in Dr. Tara J. Palmatier.  And if she is unavailable, I am sure she can refer you to another specialist that can help. By now, I am sure at least one person will ask the question of "Why should I care?"  Let me answer this question with some others.  What is it you are trying to create in the world?  Is it more anger, or is it more compassion? Most people will say that it is more compassion.  And I will totally applaud that motivation.  However, if you really look at what is going on, does anger create compassion, or just more anger? If someone can't say either way, which it creates, let me refer you to the past. author: Sam A. Robrin
text_post: RE: Are you letting your anger consume you? When you see injustice, it's normal to be angry; I'm not sure you can oppose it if you aren't. But whatever you do, don't deny your anger.  Coming from a Quaker/pacifist background, I've seen way too many instances of people who try to posture that they're above anger.  Some fear what God will do to them if He reads their thoughts; some just want to appear superior to others; there probably are a genuine few who are just that loving, though I'm not sure I've ever met one! The problem with that kind of repression is, it diverts you from understanding the real problems, and distracts you from finding solutions.  It also tends to come spewing out at the darnedest times, usually all over those least deserving.  I've sure learned to avoid the "St. Francis" poseurs for just that reason! So acknowledge the truth of your righteous rage, and focus it toward curing those injustices that created it.  We'll all be better off that way.

text_post: RE: Are you letting your anger consume you? Men's rights and feminism aside here, the consuming anger you're talking about could well be a recently diagnosed condition known as; 'post traumatic embitterment disorder' (PTED)  PTED is psychiatry's newest discovery - bitterness as a mental illness.  Bitterness is different from anger in as much as you feel helpless plus angry where you are just left with ruminations of fantasy revenge, bitterness truly is the frozen lake of unresolved anger.  So much anger is unresolved in the modern world taking the hypocrisy of feminism for example because deep down we know there's bugger all we can do about it.  PTED could be what a lot of modern men are feeling.  There is no medication or known cure, luckily we have a rant section here.

text_post: RE: Are you letting your anger consume you? I just joined up here this month and I'd be lying if I said I didn't come here out of anger, or at the very least, extreme frustration.  I'm still angry and frustrated but I'm not just sitting back and allowing it to consume me; I'm trying to do something about it - I'm trying make a difference by educating myself and arming myself with the knowledge necessary to effect change.  Even if that change is small I can console myself with the fact that I didn't sit back and just take it; I think standing up against injustice and inequality is a great way to resolve anger.  I try to keep it in check though.  I'm not going to change anybody's mind or convince them of anything if I'm yelling FUCK YOU at them.
